title: Amortization collapse for superchannel divergences
source:
Hirche's Remark 5.4, after Eqs.~(75)--(77), asked about amortization
collapse in general superchannel discrimination settings. His
Eqs.~(33) and (39) define the ordinary and nested amortized quantities
with a reference passing through the inserted channel
\sourcecite{ref:p68-hirche}{Hir23}.
progress:
Fang and Fawzi proved the analogous point-to-point channel collapse
  \begin{equation}
    \widehat D_{\alpha,{\rm ch}}^{A}(\mathcal N\|\mathcal M)
    =\widehat D_{\alpha,{\rm ch}}(\mathcal N\|\mathcal M),
    \qquad 1<\alpha\leq2,
    \label{eq:p68-channel-geometric-collapse}
  \end{equation}
  from a chain rule for the geometric R\'enyi divergence
  \sourcecite{ref:p68-fang-fawzi}{FF21}.
Equation~\eqref{eq:p68-channel-geometric-collapse} concerns point-to-point
channels; it does not settle the superchannel claim.

For the nested superchannel definition, the max-relative-entropy
subcase also collapses. Indeed, let
$t=2^{D_{\max,\mathrm{ch}}(\mathcal N\|\mathcal M)}$ and
$s=2^{D_{\max,\mathrm{sc}}(\Theta_1\|\Theta_2)}$ be finite.
Channel max-relative entropy is characterized by CP order, and physical
superchannels preserve that order. Thus
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal N\leq_{\mathrm{CP}}t\mathcal M
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \Theta_1(\mathcal N)\leq_{\mathrm{CP}}t\Theta_1(\mathcal M)
    \leq_{\mathrm{CP}}ts\Theta_2(\mathcal M),
  \label{eq:p68-nested-max-order}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal A\leq_{\mathrm{CP}}\mathcal B$ means
$\mathcal B-\mathcal A$ is completely positive.
Taking logarithms in Eq.~\eqref{eq:p68-nested-max-order} and using
Eq.~\eqref{eq:p68-channel-max-collapse} bounds each term of the amortized
supremum by $\log_2s$. Choosing $\mathcal N=\mathcal M$ gives the reverse
inequality, proving Eq.~\eqref{eq:p68-superchannel-collapse} for
$\mathbf D=D_{\max}$. If the unamortized divergence is infinite, the same
reverse inequality already proves equality in the extended sense.
This is a direct consequence of the cited channel CP-order characterization
\sourcecite{ref:p68-wilde-berta-hirche-kaur}{WBHK20}; it does not prove
collapse of Hirche's larger fully amortized quantities
\sourcecite{ref:p68-hirche}{Hir23}.

With slot assistance, nested amortization collapses for every pair of
finite-dimensional deterministic physical superchannels and every
$1<\alpha\leq2$. Mohr's Theorem~1 allows arbitrary joint insertions
$AR\to BR$ and an independent reference for the state tests. The equality
includes singular supports and infinite divergences. An inserted
reference of dimension $\dim(C)\dim(A)\dim(B)$ suffices for the ordinary
supremum, where $C$ is the input of the output channel
\sourcecite{ref:p68-mohr26}{Moh26}
(\href{https://github.com/Naixu-Guo/quantum-open-problems/issues/137}{GitHub \#137}).

With insertions restricted to $A\to B$, nested amortization can
strictly increase the divergence for every $1<\alpha\leq2$.
Savadatti's Theorem~1 uses two superchannels that prepare different
diagonal qutrit states, apply the inserted qutrit-to-qubit channel,
and dephase the output. At $\alpha=2$ the shared-channel optimum is
$\log_2(3/2)$, while a pair of distinct insertions achieves
$\log_2(183/116)>\log_2(3/2)$ after subtracting its channel divergence.
On the same example, an assisted insertion can retain all three input
labels in $R$, giving ordinary and nested amortized values of
$\log_2(5/3)$ at $\alpha=2$
\sourcecite{ref:p68-savadatti26}{Sav26}
(\href{https://github.com/Naixu-Guo/quantum-open-problems/issues/155}{GitHub \#155}).

comment:
The reference in the channel state tests of
Eq.~\eqref{eq:p68-channel-amortization} can be used under either slot
convention. Slot assistance also lets a register pass through the
inserted channel. Hirche's fully amortized divergence in Eq.~(40)
introduces an additional optimization, and its collapse remains a
separate question \sourcecite{ref:p68-hirche}{Hir23}.
